correctness.rationale: All algebra endomorphisms have the block form with degree-two action the tensor square of their quotient map: the algebra square ideal is the full tensor square. Simultaneous composition-idempotency and commutation yield an exact split module for the algebra generated by commuting projections over every field. A shared equivariant section produces one shear-conjugation normal form. The stabilizer consists exactly of intertwiners between joint eigenspaces, with dimension \(\sum_\epsilon n_\epsilon m_\epsilon\). Counting decompositions and shear cosets yields the stated exponent \(n^3-E\), and every nonempty subset product has rank \(r_I+r_I^2\). An separately implemented direct enumeration over \(\mathbb F_2\) for one and two generators checks every pair-rank and product-rank coefficient, including \(868\) total commuting pairs and the split \(384+96=480\). Finite checking corroborates; the splitting and orbit arguments prove the quantified theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies and counts all commuting algebra retractions of an intrinsically defined free two-step nonunital associative family for arbitrary tuple length, including the ranks of every nonempty product. This is a natural endomorphism-monoid invariant, not a single small example: simultaneous commutation forces one shared shear stabilizer coupled to the Boolean-AND tensor grading. For two generators over the binary field, pair ranks alone aggregate \(480\) cases whose product ranks differ, splitting into \(384\) and \(96\); the full statistic detects this otherwise hidden structure. No unproved downstream result is asserted.
